title: Recognising Structures
page_title: Recognising Gas Exchange Structures – CIE A Level Biology

blocks.name: Recognising Structures in the Gas Exchange System
blocks.definition: recognise trachea, bronchi, bronchioles and alveoli in microscope slides, photomicrographs and electron micrographs and make plan diagrams of transverse sections of the walls of the trachea and bronchus

blocks.text: Recognising structures in the gas exchange system

blocks.md:
- A **tracheal cross-section** shows the large lumen, which air has to travel through
- The innermost cells of the trachea are the ciliated epithelia with projections called cilia

blocks.alt: Trachea cross-section as shown under a light microscope
blocks.caption: Trachea cross-section as shown under a light microscope

blocks.md:
- The cells of the **ciliated epithelium** are shown in the light micrograph below

  - The cells are tightly packed and interspersed with goblet cells, which are shown in light grey

blocks.alt: A light micrograph image showing tissue of the trachea
blocks.caption: A photomicrograph image showing tissue of the trachea

blocks.md:
- The density of the** cilia** are shown in the electron micrograph below

  - The cilia are essential for sweeping bacteria and dust-filled mucus away from the lungs and up the trachea into the back of the mouth
  - This mucus is then swallowed, with any pathogens hopefully destroyed by the acidic conditions in the stomach

blocks.caption: An electron micrograph of the tissues that can be found inside the trachea

blocks.md:
- **Bronchi** are distinctive from the trachea because their lumen is narrower (around 8-9mm instead of 18mm
- However, like the trachea, they are lined by ciliated epithelium

blocks.alt: A light micrograph image showing tissue of the bronchi in cross section
blocks.caption: A photomicrograph image showing tissue of the bronchi in cross section

blocks.md:
- **Bronchioles** are approximately 1mm or less in diameter
- Smooth muscle and cuboidal epithelium are found in their walls

blocks.alt: A photomicrograph showing bronchiole tissues in the gas exchange system
blocks.caption: A photomicrograph showing bronchiole tissues in the gas exchange system

blocks.md:
- Alveoli have a sponge-like appearance under a microscope due to their air spaces.
- They are surrounded by an extensive capillary network and are lined by squamous epithelium

blocks.alt: The cells surrounding the alveolus air sac as viewed by a light microscope
blocks.caption: The cells surrounding the alveolus air sac as viewed by a light microscope

blocks.text: Walls of the trachea and bronchus

blocks.md:
- The tracheal lumen is around 15 to 20 mm and is lined by ciliated epithelia
- The tracheal wall is surrounded by strong and flexible cartilage which flexes during breathing
- The smooth muscle of the trachea constricts and allows air to be expelled with more force

blocks.alt: Cross-section diagram of the trachea showing labels for smooth muscle fibres, ciliated epithelium with glands, lumen, wall, cartilage, and connective tissue.
blocks.caption: Labelled diagram of a cross section of the trachea

blocks.md:
- Like the trachea, the **bronchus **is lined with ciliated epithelium
- The cartilage hoops provide structural support to the bronchi and the gland ducts secrete mucus in the bronchial tubes

blocks.alt: Cross-section diagram of a bronchus showing labelled sections: airway, cartilage hoop, gland ducts, ciliated lining, and surrounding tissue features.
blocks.caption: Parts of the cross section of a bronchus. This would be the same in both bronchi
